title: Dementia: type, stage and behavior
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cognitive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for dementia and behavioral changes.

HPI
The patient is a 66-year-old male presenting for a follow-up evaluation of his Alzheimer's disease. He is currently experiencing a mild stage of cognitive decline. His daughter reports that the patient has been increasingly agitated during the evening hours, leading to difficulty with his daily routine. He remains functional during the day but becomes noticeably distressed at night.

Medication List
Donepezil 10mg daily
Memantine 5mg twice daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person and place, but shows some disorientation to time. He is cooperative but appears slightly agitated during the interview. Speech is clear. Gait is steady.

Assessment
1. Alzheimer's disease, currently presenting as mild dementia.
2. Evening agitation.

Plan
We will continue the current medications for cognitive support. To address the evening agitation, we will initiate a low-dose sedative to be administered at sundown. We will monitor for effectiveness and side effects at the next visit. The daughter was instructed on safety measures for the home.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Alzheimer's disease: G30.9, sequenced first; the dementia is then coded with F02.- (dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere).
Alzheimer's disease (F02.-, dementia in other diseases), mild, with agitation: F02.A11.

distractors.why: F02.- is a manifestation code: code first the underlying Alzheimer's disease (G30.9).
The provider documents the stage (mild): it decides the code and the HCC.
Agitation is documented: use the 'with agitation' code.
Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease is F02.- (in other diseases), not F03.- (unspecified dementia).
